chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Indeed, upon one of you, when the night has passed halfway, is to rise and pray his prayer as a single unit of thirteen rak'ahs. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and supplicate; and if he wishes, he may sleep; and if he wishes, he may go wherever he wishes."
ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are prescribed for the night prayer after the middle of the night according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Baqir (AS) via the chain of Zurarah, this hadith codifies the specific structure of the night prayer as thirteen rak'ahs performed as a single, uninterrupted unit after midnight. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the continuity of worship while granting flexibility in the post-prayer state, allowing the believer to choose between spiritual engagement through supplication or rest. This ruling underscores the balance between rigorous devotion and practical ease in the performance of Sunnah prayers.
